title: When the Ember Burns Revisited
premise: Jonah Dunmore, a temple scribe bound by debt to the Order of the Quiet Flame, has spent seven years selling harmless charms in a city where magic is outlawed—until the border wards collapse and the stars go dark on the same night. The wards were fed by souls sold to the court beneath the mountain, and among them is the soul of Wren, the ember-keeper Jonah loved and lost years ago, whose memory has been erased from every record but Jonah's own hidden notes. To restore light and law, Jonah must descend into the mountain court and steal Wren's soul back before it is burned as fuel for a new, tyrannical ward. In the end, Jonah succeeds only by offering their own name-memory in exchange: Wren returns to the world whole, but Jonah must relearn who they are from the person they saved—and chooses love freely given over duty freely abandoned.
about_author: Sebastian Oyelaran is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing confiscated grimoires before turning to fiction. They write quiet, aching fantasies about people caught between institutions and the ones they love.

chapters.title: The Price of Small Lights
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. We meet them hawking charms in Ashmarket, hiding their gift behind ledger-work for the Order that owns their debt. A child buys a charm that shouldn't work—and does. Emotional beat: weary tenderness masking fear of discovery.

chapters.title: The Night Without Stars
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. The border wards fail at midnight; the sky goes black; panic floods the city. The Order conscripts all registered scribes, including Jonah, to assess the damage. Emotional beat: dread sharpening into reluctant purpose.

chapters.title: What the Ledger Kept
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV, with an interlude of Wren's fragmented memories surfacing unbidden. Auditing the ward-records, Jonah finds Wren's soul listed as 'asset, sold.' Their hidden notes are the only proof Wren ever existed. Emotional beat: grief reignited into resolve.

chapters.title: The Debt Collector's Bargain
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. High Cantor Vess offers to erase Jonah's debt if they surrender their notes and forget Wren officially. Jonah refuses and steals the descent-keys instead, fleeing with the child, Sefa, as witness. Emotional beat: duty inverted—betrayal of the institution becomes fidelity to love.

chapters.title: Down the Stair of Teeth
chapters.summary: Alternating POV between Jonah and Sefa. The two slip through the collapsed ward-line into the mountain's throat, navigating corridors that eat sound and memory. Sefa begins remembering things she never lived. Emotional beat: claustrophobic wonder, trust forming.

chapters.title: The Court Beneath
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. They reach the underground court, where masked magistrates trade in souls like coin. Jonah bargains under false identity while recognizing, horribly, that the court's power runs on forgotten names—including pieces of their own past. Emotional beat: vertigo of recognition.

chapters.title: Ash Where the Heart Was
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Jonah finds Wren—alive, functional, but hollowed, their soul already portioned out as ward-fuel. Wren doesn't know them. Jonah must decide whether restoring a person who won't remember you is worth everything. Emotional beat: devastating hope.

chapters.title: The Burning Hour
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The court prepares to ignite the remaining soul-shards to forge a new ward and seize the surface. Jonah sabotages the furnace, and in the chaos reaches Wren's core-shard just as the magistrates close in. Emotional beat: desperate, breathless climax.

chapters.title: A Name Given Back
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Escape is impossible unless someone pays the court's price. Jonah trades their own name-memory—the self that loved Wren—for Wren's release, and the mountain lets them go. Emotional beat: sacrifice rendered not tragic but chosen.

chapters.title: When the Ember Burns Revisited
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Above ground, dawn returns and the stars relight. Wren, restored but a stranger to Jonah, reads Jonah's hidden notes aloud and begins teaching them who they were—and asks, gently, who they might become together. Emotional beat: quiet, earned renewal; love rebuilt from scratch.
